text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared repository. Every time they do this, automated builds start immediately. The CI pipelines then run tests to check that the new code works correctly with the rest of the project. This process helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. Because problems are found quickly, they are usually easier and cheaper to fix. CI also saves time, since developers do not need to build or test everything by hand. In short, Continuous Integration helps teams work faster and produce more reliable software.
